points.description: States that the algorithm must be implemented, i.e. written as a runnable program/code that can be executed. Merely describing or analysing the algorithm theoretically does not earn this point.
States that the physical/actual running time of the implemented algorithm is measured, e.g. by timing its execution with a clock or timer, rather than only giving a theoretical time complexity.

levels.says: Mentions measuring or recording time, but does not make clear that it is the actual/physical running time of the executed implementation.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both implementing the algorithm as executable code and measuring its actual/physical running time. Part marks on P2 are available for a vague statement about measuring time without specifying actual execution timing. No marks are earned for purely theoretical analysis or for describing the algorithm without implementing and timing it.
